title: SC-300 Domain 2 questions (2.1, 2.2)
note: Original questions written for Delzar Certification Academy. Not from exam dumps or commercial banks; not affiliated with Microsoft.

questions.stem: After the retirement of the legacy MFA and SSPR method settings, where does a Microsoft Entra administrator control which authentication methods users can register and use for both MFA and password reset?
choices: The per-user MFA service settings
The self-service password reset policy
The Conditional Access grant controls
The Authentication methods policy
questions.answer: The Authentication methods policy
questions.explanation: Microsoft converged method management into the Authentication methods policy, which now governs methods for both MFA and SSPR. Conditional Access decides when strong authentication is required, not which methods exist.

questions.stem: Fabrikam wants to make Microsoft Authenticator available only to a pilot group of IT staff before rolling it out to everyone. What should you do?
choices: Enable legacy per-user MFA for each member of the pilot group
Create a Conditional Access policy that requires MFA for the group
Enable Authenticator for the pilot group in the methods policy
Turn on security defaults and exclude users outside the pilot
questions.answer: Enable Authenticator for the pilot group in the methods policy
questions.explanation: Each method in the Authentication methods policy can be targeted at specific groups, which is how you pilot a method. A Conditional Access policy requiring MFA does not control which methods a user is allowed to register.

questions.stem: Many Tailspin Toys users still rely on text messages for MFA. Admins want users to be prompted during sign-in to set up Microsoft Authenticator, with a limited number of chances to postpone. What should you configure?
choices: A Conditional Access policy requiring a compliant device
A registration campaign in the Authentication methods policy
Security defaults with text message sign-in disabled
An SSPR reconfirmation interval for registered methods
questions.answer: A registration campaign in the Authentication methods policy
questions.explanation: A registration campaign in the Authentication methods policy nudges users who have not set up Microsoft Authenticator during sign-in and can limit how many times they snooze the prompt. An SSPR reconfirmation interval only asks users to confirm methods they already registered.

questions.stem: Users at Adatum have both text message codes and passkeys registered, but most keep choosing the text message option at sign-in. Admins want Microsoft Entra ID to prompt each user with the most secure method they have registered. What should be enabled?
choices: System-preferred multifactor authentication
Number matching for push notifications
Registration enforcement for SSPR
A default sign-in method chosen by each user
questions.answer: System-preferred multifactor authentication
questions.explanation: System-preferred MFA makes Microsoft Entra ID prompt for the strongest method a user has registered instead of the user's own default. Number matching hardens push approvals but does not change which method is offered.

questions.stem: Relecloud is planning its authentication strategy and wants to start by removing phishable methods for its administrators. Which methods should the plan require for administrator sign-ins?
choices: Text message or voice call verification
OATH time-based software tokens
Authenticator push with number matching
Passkeys (FIDO2) or Windows Hello for Business
questions.answer: Passkeys (FIDO2) or Windows Hello for Business
questions.explanation: Passkeys and Windows Hello for Business are phishing-resistant because the credential is bound to the legitimate sign-in origin. Authenticator push with number matching is stronger than codes, but a user can still be tricked into approving a real-time phishing proxy.

questions.topic: Temporary Access Pass and certificate-based authentication
questions.stem: Which statement BEST describes a Temporary Access Pass in Microsoft Entra ID?
choices: A one-time code sent by text message that lets a user reset a forgotten password
A time-limited passcode that satisfies strong authentication requirements
A guest invitation link that expires after it is redeemed by the guest
A short-lived refresh token issued after MFA succeeds
questions.answer: A time-limited passcode that satisfies strong authentication requirements
questions.explanation: A Temporary Access Pass is an admin-issued, time-limited passcode that counts as strong authentication, so users can onboard or recover passwordless methods. It is not a password reset code and not a token.

questions.topic: Temporary Access Pass and certificate-based authentication
questions.stem: Woodgrove Bank ships FIDO2 security keys to new hires, who have no other registered method on their first day. The company wants new hires to register the keys without ever using a password. What should you do?
choices: Enable text message sign-in for new hires
Exclude new hires from MFA for their first week
Issue each new hire a Temporary Access Pass
Give new hires a temporary password and per-user MFA
questions.answer: Issue each new hire a Temporary Access Pass
questions.explanation: A Temporary Access Pass lets a user sign in strongly and register a passkey without a password. Excluding new hires from MFA leaves the accounts exposed and still relies on a password.

questions.topic: Temporary Access Pass and certificate-based authentication
questions.stem: A help desk technician must create Temporary Access Passes for standard users who are not administrators. Which role should you assign by following the principle of least privilege?
choices: Authentication Administrator
Privileged Authentication Administrator
Global Administrator
Authentication Policy Administrator
questions.answer: Authentication Administrator
questions.explanation: Authentication Administrator can manage authentication methods, including issuing a Temporary Access Pass, for non-administrator users. Privileged Authentication Administrator can also do it, but it covers administrators too and is broader; Authentication Policy Administrator manages the policy, not individual users' methods.

questions.topic: Temporary Access Pass and certificate-based authentication
questions.stem: An admin issues a Temporary Access Pass to a user who only needs to sign in once to register Windows Hello for Business. The pass must stop working immediately after that sign-in. What should the admin configure?
choices: Set the pass to one-time use
Set the pass to the longest allowed lifetime
Require the pass to be sent by text message
Add the user to a Conditional Access exclusion group
questions.answer: Set the pass to one-time use
questions.explanation: A one-time use Temporary Access Pass is consumed by the first sign-in, so it cannot be reused. A longer lifetime does the opposite and keeps the pass valid for longer.

questions.topic: Temporary Access Pass and certificate-based authentication
questions.stem: Litware wants employees to sign in to Microsoft Entra ID directly with smart card certificates issued by its own PKI, without federating to AD FS. What should be configured FIRST?
choices: Federate the domain to AD FS and enable certificate sign-in there
Enable password hash synchronization for all smart card users
Require a compliant device in Conditional Access
Add the issuing certificate authorities to Microsoft Entra ID
questions.answer: Add the issuing certificate authorities to Microsoft Entra ID
questions.explanation: Native certificate-based authentication validates user certificates against certificate authorities you trust in Microsoft Entra ID, so the CA chain must be added first. AD FS is exactly what native CBA lets the company avoid.

questions.topic: Temporary Access Pass and certificate-based authentication
questions.stem: Litware's PKI issues user certificates under two policies: one for smart cards and one for software certificates on laptops. Only smart card certificates should satisfy multifactor authentication. What should you configure?
choices: A username binding rule mapping RFC822Name to UPN
A certificate revocation list for each issuing CA
An authentication binding rule based on the policy OID
A Conditional Access policy requiring a hybrid joined device
questions.answer: An authentication binding rule based on the policy OID
questions.explanation: Authentication binding rules decide whether a certificate counts as single-factor or multifactor, and they can match the issuer or the certificate policy OID. Username binding only maps a certificate field to a user account.

questions.topic: Passkeys and Windows Hello for Business
questions.stem: Contoso's security team has approved one model of FIDO2 security key. Users must not be able to register any other model as a passkey. What should you configure in the passkey (FIDO2) method settings?
choices: A Conditional Access filter for devices
Key restrictions that allow only the approved AAGUIDs
A custom banned password list for key names
Self-service setup turned off for all users
questions.answer: Key restrictions that allow only the approved AAGUIDs
questions.explanation: Key restrictions use the authenticator's AAGUID to allow or block specific models, and attestation can be enforced so the model claim is verified. A device filter applies to the computer signing in, not the security key.

questions.topic: Passkeys and Windows Hello for Business
questions.stem: Which statement about Windows Hello for Business is correct?
choices: The PIN is synchronized to Microsoft Entra ID and checked like a password
It requires a FIDO2 security key plugged into the device
It works only on devices joined to an on-premises domain
The credential is bound to the device and unlocked by a PIN or biometric
questions.answer: The credential is bound to the device and unlocked by a PIN or biometric
questions.explanation: Windows Hello for Business creates a key pair protected by the device (normally its TPM), and the PIN or biometric only unlocks it locally. The PIN never leaves the device, which is why it is safer than a password.

questions.topic: Passkeys and Windows Hello for Business
questions.stem: Northwind Traders has hybrid joined Windows devices and wants to deploy Windows Hello for Business with single sign-on to on-premises file servers. The company does not want to deploy or manage a PKI for this. Which deployment model should you recommend?
choices: Cloud Kerberos trust
Key trust
Certificate trust
Password hash trust
questions.answer: Cloud Kerberos trust
questions.explanation: Cloud Kerberos trust uses Microsoft Entra Kerberos to issue Kerberos tickets, so it needs no PKI and is Microsoft's recommended hybrid model. Key trust still needs certificates on domain controllers, and certificate trust needs a full PKI.

questions.topic: Passkeys and Windows Hello for Business
questions.stem: Proseware wants frontline staff to use a phishing-resistant method on their company phones without buying hardware security keys. What should you enable?
choices: Passwordless phone sign-in with Authenticator push
OATH software tokens in Microsoft Authenticator
Device-bound passkeys in Microsoft Authenticator
Text message sign-in using the mobile number
questions.answer: Device-bound passkeys in Microsoft Authenticator
questions.explanation: A passkey stored in Microsoft Authenticator is a FIDO2 credential and is phishing-resistant. Passwordless phone sign-in removes the password but is still an approval prompt, so it is not classed as phishing-resistant.

questions.topic: Passkeys and Windows Hello for Business
questions.stem: Why are passkeys (FIDO2) considered resistant to phishing?
choices: The one-time code displayed to the user changes every thirty seconds
The credential is scoped to the relying party it was created for
The user must approve a push notification on a phone
The private key is stored safely in Microsoft Entra ID for each user
questions.answer: The credential is scoped to the relying party it was created for
questions.explanation: A passkey signs a challenge only for the origin it was registered with, so a look-alike site cannot use it. The private key stays on the authenticator; Microsoft Entra ID only holds the public key.

questions.stem: A small company uses Microsoft Entra ID Free and wants baseline MFA protection for all users with the LEAST administrative effort. What should it use?
choices: Conditional Access policies
Security defaults
Per-user MFA for every account
Microsoft Entra ID Protection policies
questions.answer: Security defaults
questions.explanation: Security defaults are free and turn on a preconfigured baseline, including MFA registration and prompts, with one switch. Conditional Access and ID Protection need premium licenses, and per-user MFA is account-by-account work.

questions.stem: A tenant that now has Microsoft Entra ID P1 licenses still has security defaults enabled. Admins want to replace them with their own Conditional Access policies. What should they do?
choices: Create the equivalent policies, then disable security defaults
Keep security defaults on and add the new policies alongside them
Enable per-user MFA for all users before creating any policy
Convert security defaults into a Conditional Access template
questions.answer: Create the equivalent policies, then disable security defaults
questions.explanation: Security defaults and enabled Conditional Access policies cannot be used together, so you build the replacement policies and then turn security defaults off. Keeping both on is not supported.

questions.stem: Users at Bellows College have received MFA prompts they did not start. Admins want users to be able to flag these prompts so that the account is treated as risky and can be acted on. What should be enabled?
choices: Number matching for push notifications
Account lockout after denied MFA prompts
Report suspicious activity
Notify users on password resets
questions.answer: Report suspicious activity
questions.explanation: Report suspicious activity lets a user flag an unexpected MFA prompt; the user is then marked as high risk for ID Protection and risk-based policies. Number matching is already enforced for Authenticator push and does not report anything.

questions.stem: Some Contoso users still have legacy per-user MFA set to Enforced, and the company now requires MFA through Conditional Access. What does Microsoft recommend for the per-user MFA setting?
choices: Keep per-user MFA enforced as a fallback for all users
Replace it with remembering MFA on trusted devices
Add the office IP ranges to the legacy MFA trusted IPs list
Disable per-user MFA once Conditional Access requires MFA
questions.answer: Disable per-user MFA once Conditional Access requires MFA
questions.explanation: Per-user MFA prompts on every sign-in regardless of Conditional Access conditions, so it can conflict with the policy design and should be turned off once policies cover MFA. Legacy trusted IPs are better replaced by named locations.

questions.stem: When self-service password reset is configured for users, what applies to administrator accounts regardless of those settings?
choices: The same single-method policy that is configured for standard users
Self-service reset is always blocked for administrator accounts in the tenant
A strong two-method policy that does not allow security questions
Administrators may reset using security questions only
questions.answer: A strong two-method policy that does not allow security questions
questions.explanation: Microsoft enforces its own strong default policy for administrator roles, requiring two methods and not allowing security questions. The settings you choose for users do not weaken it.

questions.stem: Hybrid users at Fabrikam reset their passwords with SSPR, but the new password does not work when they sign in to domain-joined computers. What should you configure?
choices: Pass-through authentication agents on two servers
Seamless single sign-on for domain-joined computers
Password hash synchronization every two minutes
Password writeback in Entra Connect Sync or Cloud Sync
questions.answer: Password writeback in Entra Connect Sync or Cloud Sync
questions.explanation: Password writeback sends a password reset in the cloud back to on-premises Active Directory, which is where domain sign-ins are checked. Password hash synchronization only flows from on-premises to the cloud.

questions.stem: Contoso wants to try SSPR with the help desk team before enabling it for everyone. What should you do?
choices: Set SSPR to All and block the other users with Conditional Access
Set SSPR to Selected and choose a group with the help desk team
Issue a Temporary Access Pass to each help desk member
Enable per-user MFA for the help desk team members
questions.answer: Set SSPR to Selected and choose a group with the help desk team
questions.explanation: SSPR can be scoped to a selected group, which is the supported way to pilot it. Conditional Access cannot be used to switch SSPR off for some users.

questions.stem: Admins notice that many users registered SSPR phone numbers years ago that are no longer valid. They want users to periodically confirm their registered information. Which setting should they change?
choices: The number of days before users must reconfirm their information
The number of authentication methods required to reset a password
Notifying users when their password is reset
Whether users can reset their password from the Windows sign-in screen
questions.answer: The number of days before users must reconfirm their information
questions.explanation: When registration is required, the reconfirmation interval makes users review their registered methods after a set number of days. The number of methods required controls the reset itself, not how current the data is.

questions.stem: Auditors at Wingtip Toys require that one stolen phone must not be enough to reset a user's password through SSPR. What should you configure?
choices: Require two methods to reset a password
Disable the mobile app notification method
Shorten the reconfirmation interval to 30 days
Allow only security questions for reset
questions.answer: Require two methods to reset a password
questions.explanation: Requiring two methods means an attacker needs more than one factor, such as the phone and an email account, to reset a password. Shortening reconfirmation does not stop someone who holds the phone today.

questions.stem: The security team wants every administrator to be alerted when another administrator resets their own password with SSPR. Which notification setting should you enable?
choices: Notify users on password resets
Require users to register when signing in
Notify all admins when other admins reset their password
Report suspicious activity for MFA prompts
questions.answer: Notify all admins when other admins reset their password
questions.explanation: This SSPR notification emails all administrators when an admin resets their password, which highlights possible misuse of privileged accounts. Notifying users only tells the person whose password changed.

questions.stem: An admin blocked sign-in for a departing cloud-only user, but the user still has access to SharePoint through an existing session. What should the admin do NEXT?
choices: Reset the user's password and wait for it to sync
Revoke the user's sessions to invalidate refresh tokens
Remove the user's Microsoft Entra ID P1 and Microsoft 365 licenses
Delete all of the user's registered authentication methods
questions.answer: Revoke the user's sessions to invalidate refresh tokens
questions.explanation: Blocking sign-in stops new sign-ins, but issued refresh tokens and existing sessions can continue until they are revoked. Removing a license does not end sessions and can take time to affect the service.

questions.stem: A user synchronized from on-premises Active Directory by Microsoft Entra Connect Sync is leaving the company. Where should the account be disabled so the change is not overwritten?
choices: Only in Microsoft Entra ID
Only in the Microsoft 365 admin center
In the Microsoft Entra Connect sync rules
In on-premises Active Directory
questions.answer: In on-premises Active Directory
questions.explanation: For a synchronized user, on-premises Active Directory is the source of authority, so disabling it there is what persists through each sync cycle. A change made only in Microsoft Entra ID to a synced attribute can be overwritten.

questions.stem: After an admin revokes a user's sessions, which capability lets Exchange Online and SharePoint Online reject the user's access tokens in near real time instead of waiting for the tokens to expire?
choices: Sign-in frequency set to every time
Continuous access evaluation
Persistent browser session set to never
A configurable token lifetime policy
questions.answer: Continuous access evaluation
questions.explanation: Continuous access evaluation lets supported services receive critical events such as session revocation and reject tokens right away. Sign-in frequency only affects when the next reauthentication is asked for.

questions.stem: An employee's company laptop was stolen, but the employee is staying with the company. The admin wants to force sign-in again on every app and stop the laptop from being used to get tokens. What should the admin do?
choices: Revoke the user's sessions and disable the stolen device
Delete the user account and create a new one
Block sign-in for the user until the laptop is found
Remove all licenses and reset all MFA methods
questions.answer: Revoke the user's sessions and disable the stolen device
questions.explanation: Revoking sessions invalidates the user's refresh tokens, and disabling the device object stops it from getting device-based tokens, while the user keeps working on a new device. Blocking or deleting the account is far more disruptive.

questions.topic: Password protection and Microsoft Entra Kerberos
questions.stem: Contoso wants to stop users from choosing passwords that contain the company name or its product names. What should you configure?
choices: Lower the smart lockout threshold
Set passwords to expire every 30 days
Add the terms to the global banned list
Add the terms to the custom banned password list
questions.answer: Add the terms to the custom banned password list
questions.explanation: The custom banned password list lets you add organization-specific terms, which are evaluated together with Microsoft's global list. The global banned password list is maintained by Microsoft and cannot be edited.

questions.topic: Password protection and Microsoft Entra Kerberos
questions.stem: Microsoft Entra password protection DC agents are deployed on-premises with the policy in Audit mode. What happens when a user sets a password that violates the policy?
choices: The password is rejected and the user is notified
The account is locked until an admin unlocks it
The password is accepted and the violation is logged
The password is accepted only for cloud sign-ins
questions.answer: The password is accepted and the violation is logged
questions.explanation: Audit mode logs what would have been rejected without blocking anything, so you can measure impact before switching to Enforced mode. Rejection only happens in Enforced mode.

questions.topic: Password protection and Microsoft Entra Kerberos
questions.stem: Attackers are spraying passwords against Litware accounts from unfamiliar IP addresses, while employees signing in from usual locations should not be locked out. Which Microsoft Entra feature is designed for this?
choices: Custom banned password list
Smart lockout
Password writeback
Seamless single sign-on
questions.answer: Smart lockout
questions.explanation: Smart lockout locks out attackers after repeated failures while tracking familiar and unfamiliar sign-in locations, so legitimate users can continue. A banned password list helps with weak passwords but does not lock anything.

questions.topic: Password protection and Microsoft Entra Kerberos
questions.stem: Users sign in to Microsoft Entra joined Windows devices with FIDO2 security keys and need single sign-on to on-premises file shares. What must admins create in each Active Directory domain?
choices: An Active Directory Certificate Services CA
A pass-through authentication agent
A Microsoft Entra Kerberos server object
A cross-tenant access policy for the domain
questions.answer: A Microsoft Entra Kerberos server object
questions.explanation: The Microsoft Entra Kerberos server object lets Microsoft Entra ID issue Kerberos tickets for the domain, so passwordless users can reach on-premises resources. A certificate authority is not required for this scenario.

questions.topic: Password protection and Microsoft Entra Kerberos
questions.stem: With Microsoft Entra Kerberos for hybrid identities, what does Microsoft Entra ID issue to a user who signs in with a passkey or Windows Hello for Business?
choices: A full ticket-granting ticket signed with the on-premises domain KRBTGT key
An NTLM hash that domain controllers accept for the user
A SAML token that on-premises domain controllers trust
A partial ticket-granting ticket that a domain controller exchanges
questions.answer: A partial ticket-granting ticket that a domain controller exchanges
questions.explanation: Microsoft Entra ID issues a partial TGT for the on-premises domain, and an on-premises domain controller exchanges it for a full TGT. Microsoft Entra ID never holds the domain's real KRBTGT key.

questions.stem: Match each authentication method to the description that BEST fits it.

pairs.match: Time-limited passcode for onboarding or recovery
X.509 certificate validated against a trusted CA
Approval prompt with number matching on a phone

pairs.item: Passkey on a FIDO2 security key

pairs.match: One-time code sent to a mobile number

targets_extra: Password hash checked by an on-premises domain controller
questions.explanation: Each method is managed in the Authentication methods policy: a Temporary Access Pass is a time-limited passcode, CBA checks a certificate chain, Authenticator push uses number matching, and FIDO2 keys can be restricted by AAGUID. A password hash check is not a Microsoft Entra authentication method.

questions.stem: Contoso is replacing security defaults with Conditional Access policies that require MFA. Which TWO actions should be part of the plan?
choices: Assign Microsoft Entra ID P1 licenses to the users in scope
Exclude emergency access accounts from the new policies
Enforce per-user MFA for every administrator
Allow only text message codes for MFA
Add the office IP ranges to the legacy trusted IPs list
answers: Assign Microsoft Entra ID P1 licenses to the users in scope
Exclude emergency access accounts from the new policies
questions.explanation: Conditional Access needs Entra ID P1 for the users it covers, and emergency access accounts must be excluded to avoid a lockout. Per-user MFA and legacy trusted IPs are older settings that conflict with a policy-based design.

questions.stem: A hybrid user synchronized from on-premises Active Directory must lose access immediately. Put the steps in the order Microsoft recommends.
items: Disable the account in on-premises Active Directory
Reset the user's on-premises password twice
Block sign-in for the user in Microsoft Entra ID
Revoke the user's Microsoft Entra sessions
questions.explanation: Microsoft's emergency guidance starts at the source of authority (disable the AD account and reset its password twice), then blocks the cloud account so it does not wait for sync, then revokes refresh tokens and finally disables the user's devices so they cannot obtain new tokens.

questions.topic: Password protection and Microsoft Entra Kerberos
questions.stem: Put the steps in order to deploy Microsoft Entra password protection for on-premises Active Directory.
items: Install the proxy service on a member server with outbound internet access
Register the proxy and the Active Directory forest with Microsoft Entra ID
Install the DC agent on the domain controllers
Run the policy in Audit mode and review the event logs
Switch the policy to Enforced mode
questions.explanation: The proxy relays the banned password policy from Microsoft Entra ID, so it must be installed and registered with the forest before DC agents can download policy. Audit mode shows the impact before Enforced mode starts rejecting weak passwords.

questions.stem: What is the minimum Microsoft Entra license needed for users who are covered by Conditional Access policies?
choices: Microsoft Entra ID Free
Microsoft Entra ID P2
Microsoft Entra ID Governance
Microsoft Entra ID P1
questions.answer: Microsoft Entra ID P1
questions.explanation: Conditional Access is a Microsoft Entra ID P1 feature. P2 adds risk-based conditions from ID Protection, but it is not needed for standard policies.

questions.stem: Fabrikam is designing Conditional Access policies that apply to all users. Which accounts should be excluded from every policy to avoid locking the organization out?
choices: All members of the Global Reader role
All users signing in from trusted locations
Emergency access accounts
All users who hold Entra ID P2 licenses
questions.answer: Emergency access accounts
questions.explanation: Excluding emergency access accounts from policies keeps a way back in if a policy is misconfigured or an MFA service fails. Excluding trusted locations would weaken policies for everyone in the office.

questions.stem: Contoso wants users to complete MFA when they register MFA or SSPR methods, unless they are on the trusted office network. What should the policy target?
choices: The Register security information user action
The Register or join devices user action
The Microsoft Admin Portals resource
The Office 365 resource group
questions.answer: The Register security information user action
questions.explanation: The Register security information user action covers combined MFA and SSPR registration, and a location condition can exclude the trusted network. Register or join devices applies to device registration, not security info.

questions.stem: Adatum wants to block sign-ins from countries where it has no operations. What should you use in the policy?
choices: The device platforms condition for those countries
A named location of countries in the Locations condition
A sign-in risk condition set to high
A filter for devices on a country attribute
questions.answer: A named location of countries in the Locations condition
questions.explanation: Named locations can be defined by country or region and used in the Locations condition with a block grant. Sign-in risk measures suspicious behavior, not geography, and needs P2 licenses.

questions.stem: A service principal used by a nightly job should only be able to get tokens from the company's data center IP range. Which Conditional Access configuration meets this?
choices: Target the app as a resource and require multifactor authentication for it
Assign the policy to the workload identity with a location condition
Add the service principal to a group and require a compliant device for it
Apply a sign-in frequency session control to the principal
questions.answer: Assign the policy to the workload identity with a location condition
questions.explanation: Conditional Access for workload identities can include single-tenant service principals and block them outside named locations; this needs Microsoft Entra Workload ID Premium. A service principal cannot perform MFA or present a compliant device.

questions.stem: Northwind wants to stop device code flow sign-ins for everyone except a few conference room devices that need it. Which condition should the policy use?
choices: Authentication flows
Client apps
Device platforms
User risk
questions.answer: Authentication flows
questions.explanation: The authentication flows condition controls device code flow and authentication transfer, so you can block it and exclude the few devices that need it, for example with a filter for devices. The client apps condition is used for legacy authentication protocols.

questions.stem: A user is included in a Conditional Access policy that blocks access and is also a member of a group excluded from that policy. What happens when the user signs in?
choices: The user is blocked because a block access control always wins
The user must complete MFA instead of being blocked
The result depends on which group was added first
The policy does not apply because exclusions take precedence
questions.answer: The policy does not apply because exclusions take precedence
questions.explanation: In Conditional Access an exclusion always overrides an inclusion, so the policy is not applied to that user. Block does win over grant controls, but only among policies that actually apply.

questions.stem: Admins at Woodgrove must ensure administrators accessing admin portals sign in only with passkeys, Windows Hello for Business or certificate-based authentication. Which grant control should the policy use?
choices: Require multifactor authentication
Require device to be marked as compliant
Require authentication strength
Require password change
questions.answer: Require authentication strength
questions.explanation: An authentication strength such as the built-in phishing-resistant MFA strength limits which methods satisfy the policy. Require multifactor authentication accepts any MFA method, including text messages.

questions.stem: A policy grants access with Require multifactor authentication and Require device to be marked as compliant, set to require one of the selected controls. A user on a personal unmanaged laptop completes MFA. What is the result?
choices: Access is blocked because the device is not compliant
Access is granted because one control was satisfied
The user must enroll the laptop in Intune first
Access is granted only in a browser session
questions.answer: Access is granted because one control was satisfied
questions.explanation: With require one of the selected controls, satisfying any listed control is enough. If the policy were set to require all the selected controls, the unmanaged laptop would be blocked.

questions.stem: Two Conditional Access policies apply to the same sign-in. One requires multifactor authentication and the other requires a compliant device. What must the user do to get access?
choices: Satisfy both MFA and the compliant device requirement
Satisfy whichever policy was created first
Satisfy the policy with the higher priority
Satisfy either one because policies are combined with OR
questions.answer: Satisfy both MFA and the compliant device requirement
questions.explanation: Every applicable Conditional Access policy is enforced, so the user must meet the requirements of all of them. Policies have no priority order.

questions.stem: Employees at Proseware use personal iOS and Android phones that will not be enrolled in Intune. The company wants Outlook mobile access only when the app is protected by Intune app protection policies. Which grant control should you use?
choices: Require device to be marked as compliant
Require Microsoft Entra hybrid joined device
Require terms of use
Require app protection policy
questions.answer: Require app protection policy
questions.explanation: Require app protection policy checks that the client app has an Intune app protection policy, which works without device enrollment. A compliant device requires the phone to be enrolled and managed.

questions.stem: Users at Bellows College must accept the current acceptable use agreement before they can open the HR portal. What should the Conditional Access policy for the HR portal require?
choices: App enforced restrictions
A persistent browser session
A terms of use grant control
An app protection policy
questions.answer: A terms of use grant control
questions.explanation: Terms of use appear as a grant control, so users must accept the agreement before access is granted. App enforced restrictions only limit what SharePoint and Exchange allow in the session.

questions.stem: Security analysts want to monitor sessions to a SaaS app in real time and block file downloads from unmanaged devices. Which Conditional Access session control should be used?
choices: Conditional Access App Control
App enforced restrictions
Sign-in frequency
Persistent browser session
questions.answer: Conditional Access App Control
questions.explanation: Conditional Access App Control routes the session through Microsoft Defender for Cloud Apps, which can monitor activity and block downloads for supported apps. App enforced restrictions only work with apps such as SharePoint and Exchange that enforce the limits themselves.

questions.stem: What happens when a Conditional Access policy is set to report-only?
choices: It is enforced only for administrator accounts
It is enforced but user prompts are suppressed
It is evaluated against past sign-ins only
It is evaluated and logged at sign-in but not enforced
questions.answer: It is evaluated and logged at sign-in but not enforced
questions.explanation: Report-only policies are evaluated during sign-in and their would-be result is recorded in the sign-in logs, without blocking or prompting users. This lets admins measure impact before turning a policy on.

questions.stem: A user says access to a finance app was blocked this morning. The admin needs to find which Conditional Access policy caused it. What should the admin review?
choices: The directory audit logs for any recent Conditional Access policy changes
The Identity Secure Score recommended actions
The Conditional Access details of the failed sign-in in the sign-in logs
The provisioning logs for the user's account
questions.answer: The Conditional Access details of the failed sign-in in the sign-in logs
questions.explanation: Each sign-in log entry shows every Conditional Access policy evaluated and its result, so the failing policy can be identified. Audit logs show who changed a policy, not how a specific sign-in was evaluated.

questions.stem: Before changing any policy, an admin wants to know which existing Conditional Access policies would apply to a specific user signing in from an iOS device at a given IP address, without that user signing in. What should the admin use?
choices: Report-only mode
The What If tool
The sign-in logs
An access review
questions.answer: The What If tool
questions.explanation: The What If tool simulates a sign-in with the user, app, platform, location and other conditions you supply and lists the policies that would apply. Report-only mode and sign-in logs both depend on real sign-ins.

questions.stem: Admins have several policies in report-only mode and want charts of their impact across all users and apps over the past month. What should they use?
choices: The What If tool run for each user
The Conditional Access insights and reporting workbook
The audit logs filtered by policy category
The Identity Secure Score improvement actions
questions.answer: The Conditional Access insights and reporting workbook
questions.explanation: The insights and reporting workbook summarizes policy results, including report-only results, from sign-in data sent to a Log Analytics workspace. The What If tool simulates one sign-in at a time.

questions.stem: A user is not being prompted for MFA, and the sign-in log shows the MFA policy with a result of Not applied. What is the MOST likely cause?
choices: The user had already satisfied the policy's grant controls in an earlier session
The policy requires a P2 license that the user lacks
The sign-in did not match the policy's assignments or conditions
Security defaults overrode the Conditional Access policy for the sign-in
questions.answer: The sign-in did not match the policy's assignments or conditions
questions.explanation: Not applied means the sign-in fell outside the policy's users, target resources or conditions, for example because of an exclusion. A satisfied grant control would show the policy as Success instead.

questions.stem: For all resources, users on unmanaged devices must reauthenticate every 8 hours and must not stay signed in after closing the browser. Which session settings should the policy use?
choices: Sign-in frequency of 8 hours and a never persistent browser session
Sign-in frequency of 8 hours and app enforced restrictions
An always persistent browser session and a compliant device
Strict location enforcement with continuous access evaluation turned on
questions.answer: Sign-in frequency of 8 hours and a never persistent browser session
questions.explanation: Sign-in frequency sets how often users must sign in again, and setting persistent browser session to never persistent ends the session when the browser closes. App enforced restrictions limit what users can do, not how long they stay signed in.

questions.stem: An admin tries to add a persistent browser session control to a policy that targets only SharePoint Online, and the configuration is not accepted. What is the reason?
choices: Persistent browser session works only with policies in report-only mode
Persistent browser session needs a hybrid joined device grant
Persistent browser session works only for guest users
Persistent browser session requires the policy to target all resources
questions.answer: Persistent browser session requires the policy to target all resources
questions.explanation: The persistent browser session control is only supported when the policy targets all resources. Targeting a single app such as SharePoint Online is not supported for this control.

questions.stem: Only privileged access workstations, tagged with the value PAW in extensionAttribute1, may be used to reach the Microsoft admin portals. Which condition lets the policy identify these devices?
choices: The device platforms condition set to Windows only
A named location containing the PAW subnet's IP ranges
A filter for devices rule on extensionAttribute1
The client apps condition set to browser
questions.answer: A filter for devices rule on extensionAttribute1
questions.explanation: Filter for devices targets or excludes devices based on device attributes, including extension attributes, so the policy can block everything except tagged workstations. A named location identifies network ranges, not the device itself.

questions.stem: Contoso wants users to reauthenticate each time they enroll a device in Microsoft Intune, even if they recently signed in. Which session control should the policy use?
choices: Sign-in frequency set to every time
Persistent browser session set to never
Require device to be marked as compliant
Disable continuous access evaluation
questions.answer: Sign-in frequency set to every time
questions.explanation: Sign-in frequency every time forces a fresh authentication whenever the targeted resource or action is reached, which Microsoft supports for Intune enrollment. A never persistent browser session only affects whether the browser keeps the session after closing.

questions.stem: Which services support the app enforced restrictions session control for limiting access from unmanaged devices?
choices: Salesforce and ServiceNow
The Azure portal and Azure CLI
Any SAML gallery application
SharePoint Online and Exchange Online
questions.answer: SharePoint Online and Exchange Online
questions.explanation: App enforced restrictions pass device information to SharePoint Online (and OneDrive) and Exchange Online, which then allow limited, browser-only access. Other SaaS apps need Conditional Access App Control instead.

questions.stem: What does continuous access evaluation provide in Microsoft Entra ID?
choices: Access tokens that all expire after five minutes so changes apply quickly
Near real-time enforcement of critical events by supporting services
An MFA prompt for every signed-in user once an hour on all supported services
A monthly review of group memberships
questions.answer: Near real-time enforcement of critical events by supporting services
questions.explanation: With continuous access evaluation, services such as Exchange Online and SharePoint Online are told about critical events and policy changes and can reject tokens right away. It works without shortening token lifetimes.

questions.stem: Admins want Exchange Online to reject a token immediately when a user's IP address is outside the allowed named locations, even when the IP address seen by the service differs from the one seen by Microsoft Entra ID. What should they configure?
choices: Disable resilience defaults in the session controls of the policy
Sign-in frequency set to every time
A never persistent browser session
Strict location enforcement for continuous access evaluation
questions.answer: Strict location enforcement for continuous access evaluation
questions.explanation: Strict location enforcement makes CAE-capable services enforce location policies using the IP address the resource sees. Disabling resilience defaults only changes behavior during an outage.

questions.stem: Why can Microsoft Entra ID issue longer-lived access tokens to clients and services that support continuous access evaluation?
choices: The token is encrypted with the user's passkey and the device's TPM key
The service can revoke the token when a critical event occurs
The client is asked for MFA again each time it presents the token
The token is bound to a named location
questions.answer: The service can revoke the token when a critical event occurs
questions.explanation: Because a CAE-capable service can reject a token as soon as it is told about events such as account disablement, the token can safely live longer. Security comes from revocation, not from a short lifetime.

questions.stem: A user's account was disabled, but the user kept working in a third-party SaaS app for almost an hour afterwards. What is the MOST likely reason?
choices: The app does not support CAE, so its token stays valid until expiry
CAE applies only to guest users who sign in from other organizations' tenants
Disabling an account is not one of the critical events that CAE handles
CAE requires every user to have a P2 license
questions.answer: The app does not support CAE, so its token stays valid until expiry
questions.explanation: Only services that support continuous access evaluation can act on critical events; other apps rely on the token's normal lifetime. Account disablement is one of the critical events CAE handles.

questions.stem: Users must complete phishing-resistant MFA only when they open SharePoint sites labeled Highly Confidential, not for the rest of SharePoint. What should you use?
choices: A Conditional Access policy that targets the SharePoint Online resource
App enforced restrictions for SharePoint Online
An authentication context applied through the sensitivity label
Sign-in frequency set to every time for SharePoint
questions.answer: An authentication context applied through the sensitivity label
questions.explanation: An authentication context lets the label call a specific Conditional Access policy only for those sites. Targeting SharePoint Online as a resource would apply the requirement to every site.

questions.stem: When users activate the Global Administrator role in Privileged Identity Management, they must use a phishing-resistant method from a compliant device. What should you configure in the role settings?
choices: Require multifactor authentication on activation
Require a Conditional Access authentication context
Require ticket information and justification on activation
Allow permanent active assignment of the Global Administrator role
questions.answer: Require a Conditional Access authentication context
questions.explanation: PIM role settings can require an authentication context, which links activation to a Conditional Access policy that demands phishing-resistant MFA and a compliant device. The basic MFA option on activation cannot check device compliance or method strength.

questions.stem: Contoso wants anyone who updates or deletes Conditional Access policies to first complete phishing-resistant MFA, even if they already signed in with MFA. What should you configure?
choices: A policy targeting the Microsoft Admin Portals resource
PIM approval for the Conditional Access Administrator role
Protected actions linked to an authentication context
An access review of Conditional Access Administrators
questions.answer: Protected actions linked to an authentication context
questions.explanation: Protected actions attach an authentication context to specific permissions, so the linked policy is checked at the moment the action is performed. A policy on the admin portals is only checked at sign-in and does not step up for the specific change.

questions.stem: What is a protected action in Microsoft Entra ID?
choices: A role that can only be activated through Privileged Identity Management approval
An app permission that always needs admin consent
A policy that cannot be disabled by any administrator
A permission that requires an authentication context policy to be met
questions.answer: A permission that requires an authentication context policy to be met
questions.explanation: A protected action is a directory permission, such as updating Conditional Access policies, that is assigned an authentication context so the linked policy must be satisfied before the action runs. It is not tied to PIM or consent.

questions.stem: Admins at a new tenant have little Conditional Access experience and want to quickly create Microsoft-recommended policies, such as requiring MFA for administrators. What should they use?
choices: Conditional Access policy templates
Security defaults together with policies
Cross-tenant synchronization from a partner
The What If tool to generate policies
questions.answer: Conditional Access policy templates
questions.explanation: Policy templates create preconfigured policies that follow Microsoft recommendations, grouped by scenario. Security defaults cannot be combined with enabled policies, and the What If tool only simulates.

questions.stem: An admin creates a policy from the Block legacy authentication template for all users. What is the BEST practice before enforcing it?
choices: Enable it immediately for all users at once
Run it in report-only mode and review the impact
Exclude all users who use mobile devices
Turn on security defaults as a backup
questions.answer: Run it in report-only mode and review the impact
questions.explanation: Running the policy in report-only mode shows which sign-ins still use legacy authentication so they can be fixed before blocking. Enabling it immediately risks breaking older clients and service accounts.

questions.stem: A Fabrikam admin creates a policy from the Require multifactor authentication for all users template. What should the admin make sure of before turning the policy on?
choices: All users have Entra ID P2 licenses
The Authentication methods policy is off
Emergency access accounts are excluded
Per-user MFA is enforced for every account
questions.answer: Emergency access accounts are excluded
questions.explanation: A policy that targets all users must exclude emergency access accounts so the tenant can be recovered if something goes wrong. Requiring MFA through Conditional Access needs P1, not P2.

questions.stem: Admins notice Conditional Access policies labeled as Microsoft-managed that they did not create, some in report-only mode. What can the admins do with these policies?
choices: Change their state and exclude users, but not delete them
Delete them because they conflict with the custom policies you created
Nothing, because they are read-only and always enforced on all users
Rename them and change their grant controls freely
questions.answer: Change their state and exclude users, but not delete them
questions.explanation: Microsoft-managed policies can be reviewed, turned on or off and given exclusions, but they cannot be deleted. Admins are not locked out of them entirely.

questions.stem: A company wants a template-based policy that controls when and from where users can register their MFA and SSPR methods. Which template should the admin use?
choices: Block legacy authentication
Require multifactor authentication for admins
Block access for unknown or unsupported device platform
Securing security info registration
questions.answer: Securing security info registration
questions.explanation: The Securing security info registration template targets the Register security information user action, for example requiring a trusted location. The other templates protect sign-ins rather than registration.

questions.stem: Match each requirement to the Conditional Access control that meets it.

pairs.item: Stop all sign-ins from a country where the company has no staff
Allow only Intune-managed devices that meet policy
pairs.match: Require device to be marked as compliant

pairs.item: Accept only passkeys or Windows Hello for Business for admins
Give unmanaged devices browser-only SharePoint access without downloads
Make users sign in again every four hours

questions.explanation: Block access, compliant device and authentication strength are grant controls; app enforced restrictions and sign-in frequency are session controls. Persistent browser session only decides whether the browser keeps the session after it closes.

questions.stem: Put the steps in order to roll out a new Conditional Access policy safely.
items: Identify the target users and exclude emergency access accounts
Create the policy with its state set to report-only
Review report-only results in the sign-in logs and workbook
Adjust exclusions for unexpected impact and notify users
Set the policy state to On
questions.explanation: Scope comes first, including emergency access exclusions; report-only then collects real results to review, problems are fixed and users told, and only then is the policy enforced. Turning it on before reviewing risks blocking users.

questions.stem: Which TWO of the following are critical events that continuous access evaluation acts on?
choices: A user account is disabled or deleted
An admin revokes the user's refresh tokens
A user changes their profile photo
A user is added to a new Microsoft 365 group
A new app registration is created
The user's manager attribute changes
answers: A user account is disabled or deleted
An admin revokes the user's refresh tokens
questions.explanation: CAE critical events include account disablement or deletion, password change or reset, refresh token revocation, MFA being enabled for the user and high user risk. Profile and group changes are not critical events.

questions.stem: Put the steps in the order Microsoft documents to require phishing-resistant MFA before admins change Conditional Access policies.
items: Create a policy that targets the context and requires phishing-resistant MFA
Add the policy update and delete permissions as protected actions with the context
Test by changing a policy while signed in as an administrator
questions.explanation: The authentication context must exist before a policy can target it, and Microsoft has you build that policy before adding protected actions so the step-up applies as soon as the permissions are protected. Testing confirms the prompt appears.
